# How viruses are built and copy themselves

> *A virus particle carries no machinery for making energy or protein. Its structure is a delivery system for a genome, and its replication cycle uses the host cell for everything else.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Describe the parts of a virion; relate enveloped and non-enveloped structure to survival; describe the steps of the replication cycle |
| Structure | Genome (DNA or RNA, single- or double-stranded), capsid, envelope; diagram as a tree of structural types |
| The replication cycle | Flow: attach, enter, uncoat, express and copy the genome, assemble, release |
| Genome types | How a DNA virus, a positive-strand RNA virus, a negative-strand RNA virus and a retrovirus each make mRNA (a simplified Baltimore scheme as a table) |
| Anchor organisms | Influenza virus (enveloped, segmented RNA) and HIV (retrovirus), from the anchor set |
| Scenario questions | Which property of a virus explains a finding, such as survival on hands after alcohol rub |
